alternatives.name: MarkItDown
alternatives.why_not_default: In catalogs/foundation/decisions.json, the source-document-conversion entry (lines 767-815) is marked 'conditional'. It records only that the selected HTML conversion passed, and its own limitation says this does not cover the optional PDF or Office extras. The Poppler README (blueprints/convergence-practice/document-ingestion/README.md, lines 15-17) still lists MarkItDown 0.1.7 as a candidate for specific unmet needs. The pin is behind upstream v0.1.8. The packet records its evidence_kind as native_execution, and the decisions lifecycle marks its 'use' stage accepted_within_scope. I did not open that HTML receipt (portable-cli-artifacts), so I label the class by what I verified myself (source_review). Keep it for HTML conversion only.

alternatives.name: Context Hub
alternatives.why_not_default: It covers a different scope: selected curated developer documentation, not controlled ingestion of local documents. The curated-developer-docs entry in catalogs/foundation/decisions.json (lines 817-856) is conditional and limited to a named documentation gap. It cites retained native search and retrieval, and the packet labels its evidence as mixed. docs/token-native-saturation.md (lines 16 and 72) shows only the 'use' stage accepted, and its kept comparison grew by 85 tokens. There is no measured retrieval-quality comparison against this layer's fixture.

alternatives.name: Docling
alternatives.why_not_default: The only evidence is a source review. catalogs/us-equities/foundation-memory.json (foundation-docling, lines 1134-1170) states that commands are prospective and were not run, and that table and unit extraction quality is unmeasured. Model weights carry separate licences. The Poppler README (lines 118-123) says to adopt Docling only when it passes a frozen layout/OCR corpus with provenance and answer checks. That comparison has not been run, so the capability is untested rather than failed.

alternatives.name: LlamaIndex
alternatives.why_not_default: The only evidence is a source review. catalogs/us-equities/foundation-memory.json (foundation-llama_index, lines 983-1018) lists the layer as rag-pipeline, says commands were not run, and notes a README emphasis on LlamaParse with possible managed-parsing cost and data transfer. It has no ingestion or retrieval receipt for this layer, so it is untested rather than failed.

limits: I could not run commands. The QMD bench, the Poppler audit and tests/test_document_ingestion.py were not re-executed. Their paths were confirmed only by a Glob match.

I did not open the MarkItDown HTML receipt (portable-cli-artifacts), the WSL Poppler receipt (wsl-document-ingestion-20260920), the Context Hub functional receipt, or evidence/artifacts/foundation-rd-20260921/qmd-bench-output.txt. Results from those sources are taken from the decisions and evidence manifests without my verification, and cross-host Poppler qualification is unverified here.
I read only the first 80 lines of the 2026-09-19 retrieval receipt. The aggregate BM25 summary is verified, but I did not check every per-query row.
Model: the fixed field says opus/high, and the client reports the running model as claude-opus-5-5[1m]. No TypeSafe service call was made, and no inference results were supplied.
The weakest winner class is recorded as measured_comparison, which reflects QMD's diagnostic benchmarks. Its search/get step and the Poppler evidence are native CLI execution on designed fixtures.
open_gaps: The two BM25 benchmark runs differ, and neither is general. On the 2026-09-19 lexical snapshot (18 eligible and 33 FTS documents), BM25 returned 8/12 top-three hits, so 4 top-three misses. On the 2026-09-21 expanded unsealed index (131 documents, full_corpus_seal false, one ordered run), it returned 6/12 top-three and 8/12 top-five, so 6 top-three misses and 4 top-five misses. Whether expanding the index degraded BM25 ranking has not been checked with a repeated or sealed run.

The observed search-then-get body retrieval covers two selected lexical queries on one source host (native-catalog-retrieval-20260920). It does not show exact-body retrieval for arbitrary queries or for another PC.

The Poppler evidence covers one designed, born-digital, 3-page Latin-script corpus with a known table layout on the observed Mac. It does not cover OCR, arbitrary layouts, scans, Office documents, filings or other machines.
MarkItDown acceptance covers HTML only. Its PDF and Office extras are unqualified.
Docling and LlamaIndex have no executed evidence for this layer. They are untested, not failed.
Neither the embedding-model download cost nor any provider-token saving is established.

arms: QMD hybrid/vector/full on the same sealed index
Docling on the frozen layout/OCR corpus
MarkItDown with PDF/Office extras on the same corpus
overturn_protocol.metric: Retrieval: recall@1, recall@3 and recall@5, MRR, and correct absence on negative queries on a sealed corpus, measured with repeated warm and cold end-to-end latency. Also an exact-body match for search-then-get. Ingestion: exact page text, table-cell accuracy, positive and negative query answers with source/page citations, and refusal of invalid input.

overturn_when: The QMD BM25 verdict would change if a sealed, representative rerun of `qmd bench` on blueprints/us-equities/retrieval-evaluation/fixture.json, or on a successor fixture with positive and absent queries, showed hybrid, full, vector or another retriever giving useful gains in recall or MRR with acceptable repeated end-to-end latency. The same applies if an expanded-index rerun keeps BM25 top-three recall below the 8/12 baseline while another mode recovers it. The Poppler verdict would change if a separately frozen corpus of real multi-column, table-heavy or scanned pages, checked the same way as python3 blueprints/convergence-practice/document-ingestion/audit.py and tests/test_document_ingestion.py, showed Poppler failing where Docling or MarkItDown passes the provenance and answer checks.
why_selected:
This verdict comes from my own review of the source files. No TypeSafe inference results were supplied, and no provider judgment is carried over. The skill body was in context from <host-path>/typesafe-ai. The requirement is to find Markdown or document content from a controlled source and to retrieve the original body before relying on a result. Two components have observed native evidence that meets it.

(1) QMD BM25 (c5) handles Markdown, and its search-then-get step was observed in this revision. evidence/receipts/native-catalog-retrieval-20260920.json (lines 38-93) records QMD 2.8.3 running two scoped 'search ... -n 1 --format json' commands and two 'get ... --no-line-numbers' commands. All four exited 0. Each search returned the intended source first: docs/harness-defaults.md at score 0.76 and catalogs/foundation/README.md at score 0.68. Each get returned 'exact source body plus upstream final display newline', matched to pinned source sha256 values at revision 1445d1b. The receipt also records an independent review with no actionable findings. The scope is two selected lexical queries on one host.

Ranking evidence comes from two runs on different corpora, and they should not be merged. First, blueprints/us-equities/retrieval-evaluation/receipt.json (observed 2026-09-19, lines 15-25) ran the pinned upstream runBenchmark on a lexical index snapshot. The collection filter limited results to 18 foundation sources, while BM25 statistics used 33 FTS documents. BM25 scored recall@1 0.5, recall@3 0.667 (8 of 12, so 4 top-three misses), recall@5 0.75 and MRR 0.610. manifests/evidence.json lines 832 and 839 give the same figures. Second, evidence/artifacts/foundation-rd-20260921/qmd-comparison.json is one ordered four-mode run on 2026-09-21 against an expanded, unsealed index of 131 documents in 5 collections. It records the embed and bench commands exiting 0; an earlier attempt that timed out (exit 124) is kept and excluded. There, BM25 scored recall@1 0.417, recall@3 0.5 (6 of 12), recall@5 0.667 (8 of 12) and MRR 0.508 at 5 ms. Hybrid matched those recall figures, with MRR 0.503 at 10328 ms. Full had the highest MRR, 0.519, but recall@5 dropped to 0.5 at 75920 ms. Vector was lower on every metric. On the expanded index, BM25 therefore had fewer top-three hits than the September 19 baseline, and the file itself notes that the 'expanded index differs from September19 baseline'. BM25 stays the default because no mode improved recall, full's small MRR gain came with a recall@5 loss and about 15,000 times the latency, and BM25 needs no embedding model.

(2) Poppler (c2) handles PDFs. blueprints/convergence-practice/document-ingestion/accepted/receipt.json (attempt 2, the Mac qualification according to README lines 3-13 in the parent directory) records native pdftotext -bbox-layout from Poppler 26.09.0. Both commands exited 0. The corpus had 3 pages and 24 table cells, and 8 positive and 4 negative queries passed with source, page and coordinate references. Invalid PDF input was refused, and every check in the receipt is true.

Together, these two components cover finding Markdown and ingesting PDFs under control. The evidence is limited to these fixtures and hosts. It does not establish general ranking or recall.
